title: Twin gyrostabilizer for a USV
imageAlt: Gyrostabilizer project hardware on an unmanned surface vehicle in a test pool
imageNote: Original gyrostabilizer project photo supplied by Affan Iman, showing the hardware and pool-test setup.
purpose: Develop and test a twin gyrostabilizer to reduce roll motion in an unmanned surface vehicle. This was my Mechatronics Engineering final-year project at Universiti Sains Malaysia, within a USM / PETRONAS Research project.
contribution: Designed and tested a twin-flywheel system using BLDC motors, servo actuation, PID control, and IMU-based state estimation. Integrated the hardware and control elements, then evaluated the system through bench and pool testing.
decisions: Mechanical and electrical integration of the flywheels, motors, and actuators.
IMU feedback and PID control for stabilization.
Experimental comparison of roll response and settling time.
verification: Under the tested conditions, maximum roll reduced from approximately 35° to 10°, and settling time from 15.85 s to 4.10 s. These figures are reported in my resume; original test plots are not yet displayed here.
